composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for Box, but the listing does not confirm every Box auth method is managed. Use your own client ID and secret in a Composio auth config, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into Box.

need_own_app.answer: For launch, yes: managed apps show Composio's name on the consent screen and share quota across Composio users. Use your own Box app if consent must show your brand or you need dedicated quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio's name with the managed app (general, not Box-specific)
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users (general)
Your own app is needed to show your brand on the provider consent screen
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval (general)

scenarios.label: Custom OAuth app, customers' admins authorize
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your own unpublished User (OAuth 2.0) app used by customers in their own Box enterprises, not listed in Box Integrations.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No documented timeline for customer admin approval; depends on each customer's admin.

scenarios.approval: No Box review of your app is documented for unpublished apps. Each customer's Box Admin or Co-Admin may need to approve or enable it.
extras: Admin approves, or enables inactive unpublished OAuth apps

modifiers.note: Admin approves, or enables inactive unpublished OAuth apps

scenarios.label: Listed in Box Integrations / partner
scenarios.when_this_applies: You want to publish your OAuth 2.0 app in Box Integrations and possibly join the Technology Partner Program.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count; the submission checklist is on a separate page not in the dossier

scenarios.approval: Listing is submitted for approval in the Developer Console and goes through a partner review. What it checks was not found.
extras: Customer Box Admin still approves enterprise use

modifiers.note: Customer Box Admin still approves enterprise use

prerequisites.title: Box Developer Console access
prerequisites.detail: A free developer account gives Developer Console access. Product availability depends on plan and entitlements; not every product is on the free plan.

prerequisites.title: Production-ready OAuth 2.0 app
prerequisites.detail: Publishing requires a production-ready app that uses OAuth 2.0. Non-OAuth integrations cannot use the standard listing flow as-is.

steps.title: Create a User app in Developer Console
steps.detail: Log in, select New App, choose User as the app type, then Create.
steps.done_when: The app exists with OAuth 2.0 credentials.

steps.title: Get Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. Box needs exact HTTPS match and rejects duplicates.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is ready to paste.

steps.title: Register redirect URI and scopes
steps.detail: Add the redirect URI under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI on the Configuration tab and choose scopes.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI and scopes are saved.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API using your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Send Client ID to customer admin
steps.detail: Submit via the Enablement tab, or give the admin the Client ID from the Configuration tab. The admin adds it in Admin Console, Platform Apps.
steps.done_when: Admin has authorized or enabled the app.

steps.title: Wait for customer admin decision
steps.detail: The Admin or Co-Admin approves or declines; you are emailed the decision.

steps.title: Submit app for listing
steps.detail: In the Developer Console, select Apps, then Submit for Approval, fill out the form and select Submit.
inputs: Submission checklist from Box Integrations page

steps.title: Wait for partner review
steps.detail: Box runs a partner review. Duration is not documented.

steps.title: Apply to Technology Partner Program
steps.detail: Apply only after the integration is live in the Box Integrations Center.

traps.title: Scope changes need re-authorization
traps.detail: Changing scopes or access level requires re-authorization before they take effect. Enterprise developers must resubmit to their Box Admin.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: With multiple URIs, the authorization URL needs a matching redirect_uri parameter, otherwise users see redirect_uri_missing.

traps.title: App type cannot be switched
traps.detail: A User OAuth 2.0 app cannot be changed to Server Authentication; create a new app instead. Server apps need admin authorization.

traps.title: API calls count against customer allocation
traps.detail: Calls from custom apps count toward the customer's monthly API allocation, including authentication requests. Partner integration calls do not.

blockers.symptom: App is inactive for a customer's users
blockers.what_it_means: Unpublished OAuth 2.0 apps may be inactive by default until a Box Admin or Co-Admin enables them.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to authorize the app using your Client ID.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the instructions and message for the admin.

blockers.what_it_means: Multiple redirect URIs are configured and the authorization URL has no redirect_uri parameter.
blockers.what_to_do: Add a redirect_uri parameter matching a configured URI.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the authorization URL against configured URIs.

evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through backend.composio.dev so Composio can capture the auth token (general, not Box-specific).

evidence.answer: To hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint, for example https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The example proxy endpoint is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect, and it forwards the OAuth callback to https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, and it must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Add a redirect proxy only when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.
evidence.answer: A redirect proxy is only needed when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.

evidence.answer: By default, the OAuth consent screen on providers such as Google and GitHub shows the text 'Composio wants to access your account' (general, not Box-specific).

evidence.answer: The fix for the Composio-branded consent screen is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Your own OAuth app should be added only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Every UI Element has a "base scope", which provides the least
evidence.answer: For Box UI Elements, every UI Element has a base scope that gives the least set of permissions needed for that element to work.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: For this reason, this "base scope" must always be present in the token exchange
evidence.answer: For Box UI Elements, the base scope must always be included in the token exchange request.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Every UI Element should have a "base scope" that encapsulates all required permissions for the UI Element to functionally work:** Any fewer permissions on the token and the basic set of operations on the UI Element won't work. This scope should always be included in the Token Exchange request.
evidence.answer: For Box UI Elements, a base scope is required for every element, and tokens with fewer permissions than the base scope will not let the basic operations work.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: feature-level scopes. Upon pairing with base scopes, feature scopes enable
evidence.answer: For Box UI Elements, feature scopes are a second tier, added on top of the base scope, that enable extra capabilities in the element.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Since feature scopes are strictly additive, you
evidence.answer: For Box UI Elements, feature scopes are strictly additive, so granting one only permits the action it corresponds to, unless the documentation notes otherwise.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: So a developer can combine multiple scopes in a token exchange request to generate a token with the desired set of functionality.
evidence.answer: Box UI Element scopes are designed to be modular and strictly additive, and multiple scopes can be combined in one token exchange request.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: So adding this scope to the token enables the specific action.
evidence.answer: Each Box UI Element scope maps to one specific action in the element, and some scopes only apply to certain UI Elements.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scope should contain the minimum set of permissions required to perform the corresponding action:
evidence.answer: Box UI Element scopes are meant to contain the minimum permissions needed for their corresponding action.

evidence.answer: In general (not Box-specific), Composio registers and maintains managed OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so the developer does not register their own.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.answer: In general (not Box-specific), managed apps share rate-limit quota across all Composio users, while a custom app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.answer: In general (not Box-specific), managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers, while a developer's own app can use shorter intervals where supported.
